sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento dell'inflazione negli Stati Uniti al 3.8% e delle tensioni geopolitiche in Medio Oriente. Il VIX è stabile a 17.86, mentre l'S&P 500 guadagna lo 0.58%. Il dollaro USA si apprezza leggermente con un DXY a 98.52. Le materie prime come il petrolio sono in aumento, con il Brent a $106.65.

The US dollar slightly appreciates with a DXY at 98.52. Commodities like oil are rising, with Brent at $106.65.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'0.98%, Shanghai in calo dell'1.52%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.58%, il VIX è sceso dello 0.06%. Il DXY è salito dello 0.05%, a 98.52 L'oro è in rialzo dello 0.15%, a 4704.8 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è in aumento dello 0.97%, a 106.65 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è salito dello 0.4%, al 4.48%. I BTP 10Y sono stabili al 3.39%.

La situazione in Iran continua a influenzare i mercati, con un aumento dell'inflazione negli USA al 3.8% e un'impennata dei prezzi del petrolio. La crisi nello Stretto di Hormuz potrebbe avere ulteriori ripercussioni sull'economia globale.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantanovemila dollari, con una variazione del -1,50% nella giornata odierna. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una salida di 233,2 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle preoccupazioni legate all'inflazione e alle decisioni future della Fed. 
  Ethereum scende del -1,53% a duemiladuecentosessantotto dollari, mentre Solana perde il -4,35% a novantuno dollari e un centesimo. BNB registra una diminuzione del -1,25% a seicentosettanta dollari e trentaquattro centesimi. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 34, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 0.98%, Shanghai down 1.52%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed up 0.58%, the VIX fell 0.06%. The DXY rose 0.05%, to 98.52 Gold is up 0.15%, at $4,704.8 per ounce. Oil is up 0.97%, at $106.65 The 10-year US yield rose 0.4%, to 4.48%. BTP 10Y are stable at 3.39%. The situation in Iran continues to influence markets, with a rise in US inflation to 3.8% and a surge in oil prices. The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz could have further repercussions on the global economy. No major macroeconomic data out today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin holds above seventy-nine thousand dollars, with a variation of -1.5% today. ETF flows have recorded an outflow of $233.2 million. This movement could be influenced by concerns about inflation and future Fed decisions. Ethereum down -1.53% to $2,268, while Solana loses -4.35% to $91.01 BNB registers a decrease of -1.25% to $670.34 The Fear & Greed Index is at 34, in Fear zone, suggests caution on investors. We await economic data out today. For more on today's themes, find full articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Trafalgar squeeze of global liquidity
articles.snippet: by Vincent Bignon, Benoit Mojon, Miguel Ortiz Serrano The severity of financial crises is exacerbated by the lack of international liquidity or the absence of a global lender of last resort. This was evident during the Long Depression (1873-1896), the Great Depression (1929-1936), and, as we show in this paper, during the 1805-1806 crisis that followed the Battle of Trafalgar. The latter took Atlantic trade routes away from Spain and cut off Europe's access to Latin American silver, the key high-powered money of the time. This silver shortage led the Banque de France to cut lending by nearly 50% within three months, deliberately tightening credit to hoard specie and restore the value of its bank notes.

articles.title: The New Era of Air and Missile Defense
articles.snippet: Modern air and missile defense is approaching a structural limit. The model that protected forces over the past two decades remains effective, but only within a narrower envelope than current threats demand. articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: Middle East War Threatens Renewable Energy Rollout
articles.snippet: War in the Middle East has reshaped near-term energy market expectations, with direct implications for hydrocarbon supply affecting power sectors across liquified natural gas (LNG) imports, oil imports, and spot gas-dependent economies, mainly in Europe and Asia. While Middle Eastern countries retain access to abundant domestic fossil fuels, the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the crisis extends disruption beyond hydrocarbons. The combination of conflict proximity, supply chain vulnerability, capital diversion, and institutional resilience…

articles.title: The Pentagon Has Less Than 8 Months to Break China’s Rare Earth Grip
articles.snippet: China moved this week to take tighter control of its rare earths producers amid an escalating tit-for-tat battle with Washington over everything from tariffs and semiconductor warfare to pressure over Iran and Hormuz. At the same time, an ominous Pentagon deadline looms large, with the entire American defense system to be banned from using any Chinese-origin rare earths materials beginning in January 2027. With fewer than eight months on the clock, Washington is sounding the alarms at full blast, and the Department of War is leading the clarion…
